fullBlockReview.assessment: The same battery, heated resistance wire and ammeter observation are retained. The added approximately constant voltage condition makes the inference from decreasing current to increasing resistance valid; it is not asserted for arbitrary conductors or changing terminal voltages.

The reference remains 0 degrees Celsius, with R_0, R, t and (R-R_0)/R_0 unchanged. t is explicitly the Celsius temperature difference from that reference, not absolute Kelvin temperature. Proportionality is now a finite-range empirical approximation.
The exact source formula $\frac{R-R_0}{R_0}=\alpha t$ and its number (9-4) are preserved. Rearrangement gives R=R_0(1+alpha t); no sign or normalization changes.

The coefficient is tied explicitly to the zero-Celsius baseline. The one-degree explanation describes its numerical effect per degree; the surrounding equation and following inverse-degree units establish that alpha itself is not dimensionless. It is not presented as a coefficient normalized to R at an arbitrary new reference temperature.

The exact 1/273 inverse-degree estimate, gas-expansion comparison and alpha>0 sign are retained. The number is attributed to the source as an empirical approximation, not a universal exact pure-metal constant. The constant/average-alpha treatment is conditional on an appropriate small interval and a valid linear approximation.

The sodium-chloride identity 食盐溶液, concentration 10%, alpha<0, negative sign, 0.02 magnitude and inverse-degree unit are preserved, including the source's two adjacent math tokens for the negative value. The modern block limits the claim to the discussed electrolyte and relevant empirical interval rather than all electrolytes or all temperatures. The source does not specify the concentration convention or calibrated temperature endpoints; neither is invented.

R=rho l/S and R_0=rho_0 l/S are unchanged. Equal l and S are justified as a fixed-geometry approximation that neglects thermal expansion, not as an exact fact about heated solids. Cancelling the common geometry factor correctly yields the intact source formula $\rho=\rho_0(1+\alpha t)$, numbered (9-5). The inherited finite-range/constant-coefficient conditions are explicitly retained.

The figure171 reference is unchanged. The straight-line description is restricted to the valid finite interval and explicitly cannot be extrapolated to arbitrary high or low temperatures. This is a text/model check, not inspection of the drawn graph.

The tungsten incandescent-filament identity and source's approximate tenfold hot/cold comparison are preserved. The modern block identifies the cold reference, avoids a universal lamp multiplier, and explicitly forbids applying the small-interval linear law to the full heating excursion.
The original fig-171 identity, empty source figure text and source reference remain exact. No figure bytes, pixels, drawing inventory or display widths were reviewed.
The caption remains exactly 图 171 and refers to the same source figure. No caption placement or visual appearance is approved.

康铜 is not replaced by a different alloy. The source estimates alpha approximately 10^-5 inverse degrees and rho approximately 10^-6 ohm metres are retained and explicitly attributed, not silently replaced by a present-day datasheet value. Composition and temperature dependence are acknowledged. Small-TCR alloy use in stable/standard and instrument resistors is consistent with the stated qualitative purpose.

Platinum wire remains the sensing material, and 白金 is correctly identified as 铂 rather than gold or a different substance. Resistance measurement requires calibration and suitable construction. The text does not assert an unlimited thermometer range or one global linear calibration; comparisons with liquid thermometers are explicitly conditional.

dimensionsAndApplicability.alpha: The relative resistance change is dimensionless, so alpha t must be dimensionless: alpha has inverse-temperature dimension. The source's inverse-degree notation is retained; one Celsius degree of temperature difference equals one kelvin of temperature difference, without converting the Celsius reference into absolute T.
dimensionsAndApplicability.resistivity: R has resistance dimension; rho has resistance times length; l/S has inverse-length dimension. Consequently R=rho l/S and both numbered relations are dimensionally consistent.
dimensionsAndApplicability.geometry: Identifying the resistance and resistivity coefficients requires negligible change of l/S. This is an explicit approximation in block7. It must not be interpreted as an exact equality for precision metrology, especially for very small-TCR alloys where thermal expansion can be comparable to the electrical effect.
dimensionsAndApplicability.negativeCoefficient: A negative coefficient permits a decreasing positive resistance over the empirical interval; it does not authorize negative resistance. Algebraic extrapolation of the preserved -0.02 example would give zero at t=50 degrees and negative values beyond, demonstrating why the stated finite-range restrictions are essential, not a prediction or an assigned valid endpoint.
dimensionsAndApplicability.empiricalValues: All retained source estimates are preservation checks, not independently measured constants for an identified modern specimen. No unprovided sample composition, saline concentration convention, fitted interval or temperature reference is fabricated.

formula95Association.assessment: The current text places the intact resistivity formula before (9-5) within the same source-bound prose object, with no intervening equation or conceptual text. The following applicability sentence refers to that relation. The saved single author flow puts the formula in paragraph9 and the number at the start of paragraph10; no selected section break separates them. The formula-number association is therefore unique at the text-logic level.
formula95Association.retainedLimitation: The numbering segmentation remains an open layout observation. This report neither resolves it nor certifies that the two paragraphs appear together on a learner card, at a particular viewport, or in actual pixels. No flow, renderer or browser was invoked.
